title: A Business Anyone Can Start Today With Just $100
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

stated_problem.quote: and homeowners either don't know how to fix them because how often do you need to fix one, or they don't have the proper tools.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Local mailbox repair and install service
idea.one_liner: Repair, straighten, repaint and install residential mailboxes for homeowners in older neighbourhoods. It is paid per job, with an option to win bulk HOA contracts and recurring maintenance.
idea.customer: Homeowners in ageing neighbourhoods, HOAs/property managers, and realtors preparing homes for sale
idea.offer: Mailbox repair, replacement and standard or brick/masonry installs; HOA-wide uniform installs and yearly maintenance
idea.revenue_model: Per-job fee (about $200-$550 standard, $800-$1,600 masonry); HOA contracts in the thousands; possible recurring HOA maintenance

key_quotes.quote: mailbox install has high competition, which isn't great, but mailbox repair has low competition and the exact same amount of search volume as mailbox install.
Someone posted, he commented, then the HOA president called him and he had a $9,000 job.
Hands down, the highest ROI marketing method that you can employ with this business is neighborhood Facebook groups and nextdoor.com.
So find those neighborhoods with the older homes that you know have broken mailboxes and run nextdoor ads only to those neighborhoods.
do not put flyers in the mailboxes. I know for this business it sounds perfect, but that's actually illegal.
Customer acquisition, knocking on doors, rocks and flyers, door hangers, Facebook marketplace, Facebook groups.

claims.quote: Dude, I did about seven or eight last summer and I told my wife it's such easy money.

claims.quote: You're going to be in it for about 100 bucks.

claims.claim: An install can be charged at $350-$550 and takes 1-2 hours

claims.claim: About $100-$200 per hour after materials
claims.quote: So, after subtracting the materials, you're looking between $1 and $200 per hour.

claims.claim: 5-6 standard mailboxes per day
claims.quote: If you're just doing standard mailboxes, you can knock out five or six of those in a day.

claims.quote: But let's say your average homeowner mailbox job is $500 and your average HOA mailbox job is $5,000.

claims.quote: You're going to spend like 20 to 30 bucks to reach like 2 to 4,000 homeowners in those neighborhoods.

acquisition_channels.details: Lurk in neighbourhood Facebook groups and Nextdoor and reply to requests; post before/after photos; use Devi to monitor keywords
Audit neighbourhoods for broken mailboxes and knock on doors immediately; network at HOA meetings
Rock-and-flyer drops, door hangers and bandit signs at completed jobs; EDDM direct mail after storms
Nextdoor/Facebook ads geo-targeted to older neighbourhoods
Google Business Profile; targeting the low-competition 'mailbox repair' keyword
Buy HOA president databases (cell, address, email) and do outbound
Realtors, and paid referral fees to handymen and landscapers

ideas.delivery: The founder does the physical work on site (digging, concrete, posts, painting, masonry), then adds crews to scale
ideas.other_uk_rules: Cold-texting or cold-calling HOA presidents' mobile numbers bought from a database would breach PECR/TPS and UK GDPR, but this is not the main channel. Bandit signs need advertisement consent under the Town and Country Planning (Control of Advertisements) Regulations 2007. The UK has few kerbside mailboxes (letterboxes are in front doors), and HOAs are mostly a US concept, so the UK market is weak.

idea.name: Novelty/custom mailbox e-commerce
idea.one_liner: Make or import themed novelty mailboxes (sports teams, holidays, engravings) and sell them online through Shopify with niche Facebook ads.
idea.customer: Affluent homeowners who want a distinctive kerb-appeal item (Pottery Barn/HGTV types)
idea.offer: Custom or imported themed mailboxes, optionally installed
idea.revenue_model: Product markup: about $150 cost plus $50 shipping, sold for $600-$900

key_quotes.quote: You can buy them from a third party vendor, but you're going to be the guy known for the weird, wacky mailboxes.
Put those up on a Shopify site and start pushing Facebook ads to them.
What do you think the cost is to point Dallas Cowboys branded mailbox ads to people that live in the DFW area?
You can even use AI image generation tools to show the homeowners what these mailboxes would look like in front of their homes.

claims.claim: Custom jobs can be priced at $600-$900 instead of $200-$400
claims.quote: Instead of charging 2 to 400 bucks, you're going to charge 6 to 900 bucks.

claims.claim: Import at $150 plus $50 shipping and sell for $600-$900
claims.quote: that sells these really random, funky mailboxes for $150, shipping is $50 in bulk and you're selling them for 6, $8, $900 just for the mailbox itself.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook ads aimed at niche geo/fandom segments (e.g. Cowboys mailbox to DFW) to find the lowest CPA

ideas.delivery: Sourced from AliExpress/Alibaba/DHgate/Temu or made by hand, shipped through a Shopify store; local installs optional
ideas.other_uk_rules: Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 (14-day returns on distance sales); UK product safety/UKCA for imports; sports-team branding raises trademark/IP risk; import VAT and duty.

claims.claim: 100% of jobs come from bandit signs
claims.quote: I have a friend that owns a tree trimming business and they get 100% of their jobs from bandit signs.

idea.name: Daniel's pressure washing
idea.one_liner: A residential pressure washing service that wins customers with rock-and-flyer bags thrown onto driveways in targeted neighbourhoods.

key_quotes.quote: He gets a rock, he gets a flyer advertising his services, he puts it in a bag, he assembles them all in his basement with high schoolers

claims.claim: Double-digit conversion rate on rock-and-flyer drops
claims.quote: He has a double-digit conversion rate with these.

acquisition_channels.details: Rock-and-flyer bags thrown onto driveways in targeted neighbourhoods

ideas.delivery: Operator does pressure washing on site
ideas.other_uk_rules: Driveway rock drops could count as littering; leaflets through doors are fine.

idea.name: Phone Restore
idea.one_liner: The host's phone and iPad repair business, paid per repair.
idea.customer: Consumers with broken phones or iPads

key_quotes.quote: But some people were not coming to us with their iPads because they thought we only fix phones.

idea.name: Facebook group keyword-monitoring tool (Devi)
idea.one_liner: SaaS that watches Facebook groups and alerts subscribers when a post matches their keywords, so service providers can reply first.
idea.customer: Local service businesses and freelancers who hunt leads in community groups
idea.offer: Keyword alerts from Facebook groups and Nextdoor

key_quotes.quote: There's one called Devi that will monitor Facebook groups for you and notify you anytime something is posted that matches a keyword that you presubmit.
Now, Next Door and Facebook hate these tools, but who cares?

ideas.other_uk_rules: Scraping personal posts raises UK GDPR lawful-basis and transparency issues, and breaks Facebook/Nextdoor terms of service, so the platforms may ban it. DMCC Act subscription rules apply to recurring billing.
